subChunks.title: SUM OVER, LAG, LEAD, FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE
subChunks.hookHtml: Beyond ranking, window functions compute running totals, compare a row to the previous row, and find first and last values in a group — without any joins or self-joins.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Running SUM / running AVG

SELECT name, xp,
  SUM(xp) OVER (ORDER BY xp) AS running_total
FROM apprentices;

The OVER with ORDER BY creates a cumulative window: each row's running_total is the sum of all rows up to and including the current row, ordered by xp.

LAG and LEAD — access adjacent rows

SELECT name, xp,
  LAG(xp)  OVER (ORDER BY xp) AS prev_xp,
  LEAD(xp) OVER (ORDER BY xp) AS next_xp
FROM apprentices;

LAG(col, n, default) returns the value from n rows before in the window. LEAD(col, n, default) returns n rows after. Default is returned if there is no such row (first/last).

FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE

SELECT name, xp,
  FIRST_VALUE(name) OVER (ORDER BY xp DESC) AS top_earner,
  LAST_VALUE(name)  OVER (
    ORDER BY xp DESC
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  ) AS bottom_earner
FROM apprentices;

LAST_VALUE quirk: by default the window frame ends at the current row, not the last row. Add ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING to get the true last.

storyBeats.text: The weekly report needs each apprentice's XP alongside the previous week's XP and the running total.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: LAG looks back one row; LEAD looks forward. Running SUM accumulates as you scroll down. These replace entire self-joins and correlated subqueries with a single readable expression. The LAST_VALUE frame trick is one of the most commonly missed details in window functions — always specify the frame explicitly.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🪄 XP progression

Return name, xp, and the running total XP ordered by xp ascending as cumulative_xp. Also include LAG(xp, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY xp) AS prev_xp.
subChunks.guidedPracticeStarterCode:
SELECT name, xp,
  SUM(xp) OVER (ORDER BY xp ASC) AS cumulative_xp,
  LAG(xp, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY xp ASC) AS prev_xp
FROM apprentices
ORDER BY xp ASC;

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the default window frame for LAST_VALUE and why you need to specify ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING to get the true last value.

questions.prompt: What does `LAG(xp, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY xp)` return for the first row?
options: 0 — the default value, since there is no previous row
NULL — there is no previous row
The xp of the last row
questions.answer: 0 — the default value, since there is no previous row
questions.explanation: LAG(col, n, default) takes a third argument: the value to return when there is no row n positions back (at the start of the window). Here, 0 is returned for the first row.

questions.prompt: What does `SUM(xp) OVER (ORDER BY xp ASC)` compute for each row?
options: The sum of all xp values from the first row up to and including the current row, ordered by xp — a running total
The total sum of all xp values in the table, repeated for every row
The sum of xp values after the current row
The average xp up to the current row
questions.answer: The sum of all xp values from the first row up to and including the current row, ordered by xp — a running total
questions.explanation: With ORDER BY in OVER, SUM uses the default frame RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. This creates a cumulative (running) total.

questions.prompt: Why does `LAST_VALUE(name) OVER (ORDER BY xp DESC)` not return the actual last name in most rows?
options: The default frame ends at the current row — LAST_VALUE within the frame up to the current row is just the current row's value
LAST_VALUE is not a standard function
ORDER BY DESC reverses the frame
LAST_VALUE requires PARTITION BY to work correctly
questions.answer: The default frame ends at the current row — LAST_VALUE within the frame up to the current row is just the current row's value
questions.explanation: The default window frame is RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. LAST_VALUE of that frame is always the current row itself. To get the true last value, expand the frame to UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING.

questions.prompt: A developer needs to compute month-over-month XP change for each apprentice. The data has one row per (apprentice, month). What is the correct approach?
options: LAG(xp, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY apprentice_id ORDER BY month) — partitioned so LAG looks at the previous month for that specific apprentice
LAG(xp, 1) OVER (ORDER BY month) — a single global window
A self-join: a.xp - b.xp where b.month = a.month - 1
A correlated subquery for each row
questions.answer: LAG(xp, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY apprentice_id ORDER BY month) — partitioned so LAG looks at the previous month for that specific apprentice
questions.explanation: Without PARTITION BY, LAG would look at the previous row globally — which could be a different apprentice's previous month. PARTITION BY resets the window per apprentice so LAG correctly retrieves that apprentice's prior month.
